column1: # Ribosome residence time per codon, Saccharomyces cerevisiae
# SOURCE     Gardin J, Yeasmin R, Yurovsky A, Cai Y, Skiena S, Futcher B (2014)
#            Measurement of average decoding rates of the 61 sense codons
# TABLE      Table 2, "Ribosome residence time at position 6 (A) and 5 (B)"
# RETRIEVED  2026-11-04, from the PubMed Central full-text XML (PMC4371865)
#            via NCBI efetch, parsed programmatically from the table markup.
#   then extract table-wrap id="tbl2". The XML itself is gitignored as
#   third-party bulk; this file is the part actually used.
# A DEFECT IN THE PUBLISHED TABLE
#   Section A lists TCC twice, with different usage and RRT values, and
#   lists no TCT. Serine is one codon short. The rows are left exactly as
#   published. scripts/validate_elongation.py detects the duplicate and
#   EXCLUDES both rows rather than inferring which was mislabelled.
#   Ribosome Residence Time: how long the ribosome lingers with a given codon
#   at the measured position, relative to expectation. HIGHER RRT means the
#   codon is decoded MORE SLOWLY. Section A is position 6, the A site, and is
#   the one used here. Section B holds only the six codons the authors report
#   at position 5 and is not used.
#   This project's elongation layer predicts which codons the yeast tRNA pool
#   serves poorly, from tRNA gene copy numbers alone. RRT is an independent
#   positional measurement of decoding speed. The layer predicts adaptiveness
#   should be NEGATIVELY correlated with residence time. See
#   section  A = position 6 (A site), B = position 5
#   aa       amino acid, as printed in the source table
#   usage    codon usage frequency as printed in the source table
#   rrt      ribosome residence time as printed in the source table
#   p        p value as printed in the source table, asterisks retained
